sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Arvernorix was an obscure Continental Celtic god. Scholars know him from only a few inscriptions. He may have been the tribal divinity of the Arverni. The Arverni were a Celtic people of Gaul. It is unclear whether the two spellings mean two separate gods. Arvernorix and Arvernus might instead name a single god. The surviving records are very few. This scarcity makes the god's true nature hard to judge. His link to the Arverni remains a reasonable guess. The name of the tribe supports the idea. Still, scholars must treat the link with caution.
